claim_being_audited: The current release can be certified on the current record because aggregate readiness passed, there were no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and the HR benefits enrollment regression can be handled through required disclosure rather than blocking certification.

concern_ledger.concern: No admissible evidence shows the current release documentation already reflects the current evaluation results, including the HR benefits enrollment regression.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: Current model card or certification packet showing the present eval batch and the subgroup regression are documented.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: The policy states certification may proceed only if current release documentation reflects current evaluation results.

concern_ledger.concern: No admissible evidence shows the material limitation for the named launch use case has been disclosed or covered by approved mitigation/risk acceptance before launch.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: Approved disclosure language in the current model card, or approved mitigation/risk acceptance tied to this regression.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: The policy requires disclosure or approved mitigation/risk acceptance for material segment weaknesses before certification may proceed.

concern_ledger.concern: The actor relies in part on prior approval context even though that approval predates the retrieval configuration change and current eval batch.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: Current-release approval or explicitly renewed approval after review of the changed retrieval configuration and current eval batch.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: A stale approval cannot establish compliance for the current release and may overstate support if treated as substantive approval evidence.

decision_criteria: Certification is compliant only if current release documentation reflects current evaluation results.
Material segment weaknesses for named launch use cases must be disclosed before launch unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance.
Prior approvals and informal monitoring notes may provide context but do not substitute for current evidence or reviewed risk acceptance.
Aggregate readiness and lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents are supportive but not sufficient when a current material weakness remains undocumented or unapproved.
evidence_requests: Provide the current release model card or certification document showing the current evaluation results, including the HR benefits enrollment regression, are disclosed.
Provide approved mitigation or risk acceptance for the HR benefits enrollment weakness if certification is to proceed without disclosure-based remediation alone.
Provide evidence that the named launch use case determination treats the HR benefits enrollment slice as non-material, if that is the basis for certification.
specific_concerns: The policy threshold for certification is not satisfied by readiness alone; the record must also show that current-release documentation reflects current evaluation results and that the material segment weakness is already disclosed or covered by approved mitigation before launch.

The evidence shows a current HR benefits enrollment regression below warning threshold for a named launch use case, but no admissible evidence shows the model card or release documentation has been updated to disclose it.
The informal post-launch monitoring comment is explicitly not reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or approved risk acceptance, so it cannot close the policy gap.
Prior approval for the same model family predates the current retrieval configuration change and current eval batch, so it cannot substitute for current-release approval support.
unsupported_claims: The actor's statement that certification is defensible on the current record is not fully supported because the record does not contain admissible evidence of current-release disclosure or approved mitigation/risk acceptance for the regression.
Any implication that prior approval plus current aggregate readiness is sufficient for certification is unsupported under the stated policy.

Any reliance on the release-thread monitoring comment as practical mitigation support is unsupported because the evidence itself says no reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or disclosure language is attached.
